text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"Clear position: \"they aren't practical in the first place\"","quality":"argument focus","description":"The essay states its claim directly and keeps returning to the same central objection throughout."},{"evidence":"Explains why \"driverless\" cars still require a driver","quality":"reasoned support","description":"It develops its position with multiple logical points instead of mostly restating opinions."},{"evidence":"Mentions warning systems, laws, and liability in separate body paragraphs","quality":"organization","description":"The essay is structured into distinct argument points that make the progression easy to follow."},{"evidence":"\"If the technology fails and someone is injured, who is at fault—the driver or the manufacturer?\"","quality":"counterargument awareness","description":"It acknowledges a serious practical problem that strengthens the argument against the cars."},{"evidence":"\"sixty car pile-up on Highway 50\"","quality":"elaboration","description":"It adds a concrete scenario to make the consequences of the issue feel more real and persuasive."}]}
